Older homes near the town center give way to ranch subdivisions and then to farmhouses on the outskirts, and the wildlife entries change with each ring. Blair.wildlife_intro:
The pattern in Blair is set by the Broad River farm and forest roads south of Winnsboro. If we had to name this town's signature jobs, they would be gray squirrels in mature pine canopy and raccoons working creek corridors.

Brick ranches from the 1960s and 1970s, older in-town homes near the center, and fast-growing subdivisions at the edges give this housing stock three distinct generations of rooflines to inspect. River and lake country surrounds these neighborhoods — creeks, coves, and wooded drains run behind the subdivisions — giving raccoons, squirrels, and bats a covered route to almost every roofline.

Every job in Blair ends the same way it should: openings found on the inspection closed in steel mesh and flashing, so the house near Broad River farm and forest roads south of Winnsboro stops advertising vacancies to the next animal that passes.
